review_scope: Read-only full visual and text review of Gerald original 28-slide ASIC interface tutorial; no native CAD changes.

coverage.notes: Original notes contain only slide numbers on four slides, with no supplementary engineering specification. Visible overlays on 3/4 obscure underlying table rows.

facts.title: Chip and recording scale
facts.statement: The visible deck describes 512 recording channels and 128 stimulation channels per ASIC, with 32 modules of 16 amplifiers and four stimulators, a 12-bit ADC per module, and eight recording DATA outputs per chip.
facts.limits: The deck is about one ASIC and an older acquisition setup; it does not define the later eight-chip board grouping or 117-contact plan.

facts.title: Recording speed
facts.statement: The tutorial states 31.25 kS/s per channel and a 32 MHz clock input. It describes a frame of 1024 returned-clock cycles with one SYNC and 16 READ intervals.
facts.limits: These are nominal functional values, without jitter, duty-cycle, propagation-delay or corner limits.

facts.title: Recording signal directions
facts.statement: The FPGA sends CLK32MHz_In, Chip_Reset and FE_RESET to the ASIC. The ASIC transmits CLK32MHz_Out, DATA[1:8], READ and SYNC to the FPGA.
facts.limits: Direction is established functionally for these named classes; it does not establish pad electrical limits or AC_IN/IMP_TST direction.

facts.title: Recording multiplexing
facts.statement: Each DATA output carries four ADCs, each of which serves 16 amplifiers, giving 64 amplifier channels per serial output. A READ interval carries one amplifier position from each of its four ADCs.
facts.limits: A complete accepted ASIC-to-electrode/physical-chip map is absent.

facts.title: Padding and bit order shown
facts.statement: The waveform labels each READ interval as 16 clock cycles of zeros followed by 48 payload cycles. It shows A1<0>, A2<0>, A3<0>, A4<0> through A1<11>, A2<11>, A3<11>, A4<11>, and the final interval A61 through A64. This establishes a diagrammed bit-interleaved, least-significant-index-first candidate stream, not four contiguous 12-bit words.
facts.limits: Obtain confirmation of ADC numeric coding, exact frame start, middle-interval order, actual first valid cycle and the interpretation of index 0 as LSB. The matrix contains label defects.

facts.title: Possible capture edge
facts.statement: DATA transitions are drawn near rising CLK32MHz_Out edges, with falling edges near the middle of the data cells. Falling-edge capture is therefore suggested by the drawing.
facts.limits: The schematic waveform is not a setup/hold specification and cannot determine final input-delay constraints or guaranteed sampling phase.

facts.title: Clock and payload arithmetic
facts.statement: At 32 MHz, 1024 clocks are 32 microseconds and 64 clocks are 2 microseconds. Four 12-bit samples occupy 48 of 64 clocks. Across eight ASICs the raw 64 DATA wires carry 2.048 Gbit/s, while packed 12-bit sample payload is 1.536 Gbit/s (192 MB/s).
facts.evidence_kind: arithmetic from tutorial and later eight-ASIC requirement
facts.limits: These are decimal rates before downstream metadata/encoding and require removal of the tutorial padding. They do not prove FPGA/link/USB performance.

facts.title: Reset functions
facts.statement: Chip_Reset resets the chip to a known state; FE_RESET resets the front-end amplifiers. The recording table lists reset time below 1.5 ms.
facts.limits: The deck does not specify reset assertion polarity, minimum pulse width, relationship to clocks/rails, or what the table reset-time measurement covers. Do not convert <1.5 ms into a required digital pulse width.

facts.title: SPI wires and destination
facts.statement: The FPGA sends programming information over SPI CLK, L, R and LATCH. L and R program stimulators and amplifier gains. The diagram shows clock idle low and a positive LATCH pulse after the transfer.
facts.limits: The name SPI does not prove a standard SPI mode. No CPOL/CPHA, maximum frequency, setup/hold, latch width or inactive power-state contract is specified. The drawing changes data and clock together and cannot qualify the sampling edge.

facts.title: Chip configuration suffix
facts.statement: The slide 26 spreadsheet screenshot states that 12 chip-configuration bits are appended to the DR stream. It gives four 3-bit fields in transmission order DR_DAC[3:1], AR_DAC[3:1], Gain_Right[3:1], Gain_Left[3:1], with bit 3 as MSB, bit 1 as LSB, and DR_DAC bit 3 sent first.
facts.limits: This supports the shown chip suffix, not an approved complete serializer. AR_DAC/DR_DAC electrical functions and allowed settings are not described. It does not specify how DL is padded during the DR-only suffix.

facts.title: SPI length evidence
facts.statement: The visible stream screenshot reaches final bit_index 2124, with blank rows below it. The stimulus configuration screenshot has separate DL_Config and DR_Config tabs, 64-channel configuration, ENABLED, four EDGE fields, CATHODIC_AMP, ANODIC_AMP and POLARITY.
facts.limits: 2124 = 64 × 33 + 12 is consistent with four 6-bit edges, two 4-bit amplitudes, one polarity bit and a 12-bit suffix, but the complete stimulus packing order, enabled treatment, left/right lengths and compatibility with the present ASIC revision are not proven. The actual workbook/generator is needed.

facts.title: Stimulation capability
facts.statement: The tutorial describes biphasic monopolar/bipolar stimulation, passive charge balancing, 128 stimulators (64 left and 64 right), four-bit current magnitude up to approximately 22.5 microamps in approximately 1.5-microamp steps, and ±10 V compliance.
facts.limits: Compliance voltage is not a logic-pin voltage rating or a power-rail wiring prescription. The plot is an example, not a guaranteed current-versus-code corner specification.

facts.title: Stimulation waveform fields
facts.statement: The waveform diagram labels four EDGE[6:1] times and ANODIC[4:1]/CATHODIC[4:1] magnitudes. GUI screenshots permit either initial polarity and multiple stimulator selections. The tutorial GUI permits pulse counts 1–254.
facts.limits: GUI limits do not establish hardware counter capacity, a clinical safety envelope, or behavior outside the shown sequence.

facts.title: Stimulation sequencing
facts.statement: After loading SPI, the tutorial asserts STIM_EN, sends a short STIM_START pulse, and asserts STIM_CHB after 64 STIM_CLK cycles. Diagrams draw STIM_EN, STIM_START and STIM_CHB as positive-going controls; STIM_CHB is shown for 1 ms.
facts.limits: These are operating-sequence examples. They do not establish default/fail-safe states, exact pulse widths, minimum charge-balancing time, interaction with resets, or what is safe when either board is off. Timing values conflict elsewhere in the deck.

facts.title: Changing stimulation patterns
facts.statement: Slide 28 describes loading different SPI sequences for successive stimulation cycles while showing a 5 ms interval between starts.
facts.limits: Exact transfer/latch deadline, update atomicity, control-command latency and allowed interaction with ongoing stimulation are unspecified.

facts.title: Recording power estimate
facts.statement: Slide 7 reports approximately 17.24 microwatts per recording channel, excluding external LDOs. For 512 channels this is approximately 8.827 mW; for 4096 channels approximately 70.615 mW. The recording table also states less than 20 microwatts per channel.
facts.limits: This is an ASIC recording estimate only. It does not size FPGA rails, high-voltage stimulation power, board losses, clock/line loads, worst-case current, current transients or complete eight-chip system power.

facts.title: Embedded nominal supply value
facts.statement: The underlying specification table preserved in the original PPTX/PDF text includes 1.5 V supply, TSMC 180 nm BCD process and 8.1 × 7 mm die. The die size is also visible on slide 1. White overlays hide the supply/process rows in the normal slide 3/4 render.
facts.evidence_kind: underlying embedded table text; partly covered in rendered slide
facts.limits: The nominal 1.5 V value is not a guaranteed VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL or absolute-maximum table, and does not establish analog/stimulation rail details. This row should not be presented as if visibly stated on slide 4.

facts.title: AC_IN and IMP_TST coverage
facts.statement: Neither AC_IN nor IMP_TST is defined in the 28 slides, visible diagrams, extracted text or speaker notes. The deck gives no electrical specification or test sequence for these two signals.
facts.evidence_kind: negative result from full-deck visual/text review
facts.limits: Keep the earlier carrier/legacy FPGA netlist evidence separate; it cannot fill the absent ASIC pin-function specification.

contradictions.title: Stimulation clock/time values disagree
details: Slide 4 says 31.25 microseconds temporal resolution, corresponding to 32 kHz.
Slide 18 says 64 clock cycles = 2 ms, also corresponding to 32 kHz.
The GUI in slides 21–24 computes each edge step as 32 microseconds, corresponding to 31.25 kHz and 2.048 ms for 64 steps.
Slides 27–28 label STIM_CLK as 60 kHz, for which 64 clocks last approximately 1.067 ms.
contradictions.impact: Do not select a stimulation clock or pulse duration from these inconsistent values. Ask for the current intended STIM_CLK and event timing.

contradictions.title: Frequency boundary differs from example
details: Slides 27–28 show 5 ms between starts, which equals 200 Hz.
contradictions.impact: The accepted repetition-rate limit and boundary conditions need confirmation.

contradictions.title: Channel matrix has duplicated and missing labels
details: In the DATA1 matrix, ADC2 top row repeats A57 and A49 from ADC1.
Across the displayed 64 entries, A49 and A57 occur twice, and A50 and A59 are absent.
Regular numbering suggests ADC2 top-left values A58/A50 and ADC3 top-left A59, but these are inferred corrections, not accepted channel mapping.
contradictions.impact: Use the first/last interval waveform to build a proposed decoder, but obtain a corrected complete channel/electrode map before claiming channel identity.

contradictions.title: Gain range differs slightly
contradictions.impact: Request the gain-code calibration table if conversion to input volts is required; do not treat either lower endpoint as an exact code map.

U01.known: Functional directions are shown for recording clocks, DATA/READ/SYNC and the named reset/SPI/stimulation controls. Underlying table reports a nominal 1.5 V supply.
U01.uncertainty: Guaranteed electrical limits and all power-state behavior remain absent. AC_IN/IMP_TST functions/directions remain unknown.

U02.known: 32 MHz recording, 1024 clocks/frame, 16 READ intervals, 16 zero clocks + 48 payload clocks/interval, and bit-interleaved A1–A4, bit 0 through bit 11 order are shown. A 12-bit DR configuration suffix and screenshot ending at 2124 bits are available.
U02.uncertainty: Need actual timing limits/capture phase/ADC coding, complete corrected channel map, full SPI serialization/workbook and stimulation timing correction. Pause/restart behavior remains unknown.

U03.known: The tutorial describes one ASIC as 32 modules with 8 serial outputs. A DATA1 map is illustrated.
U03.uncertainty: The matrix contains duplicate/missing channel labels; physical eight-chip/board/shared-clock/shared-SPI grouping remains unspecified.

U04.known: Tutorial sequence is SPI load, assert STIM_EN, pulse STIM_START, then STIM_CHB after 64 STIM_CLK cycles; diagrams show positive-going controls. Reset functions are described.
U04.uncertainty: Reset polarity/width and power-on/fault states remain unprovided. Tutorial low levels between pulses do not approve power-on pulls or brownout behavior.

U05.known: Recording ASIC estimate 17.24 µW/channel excludes LDOs; stimulation compliance is ±10 V; underlying table lists 1.5 V nominal.
U05.uncertainty: No complete analog/digital/stimulation supply tree, per-rail currents or board return allocation.

U07.known: Eight ASIC returned clock domains correspond to the tutorial output clock; 32 MHz nominal is source-supported.
U07.uncertainty: No guaranteed input timing or complete XDC/pin allocation. Diagram-suggested falling-edge capture needs confirmation and implementation timing.

U10.known: ASIC recording-only estimate can inform the assembly budget; 4096 × 17.24 µW ≈ 70.615 mW.
U10.uncertainty: This does not change unqualified FPGA workload power, FPGA converter margins or complete assembly thermal budget.

U14.known: ASIC wire stream includes 25 percent padding clocks. Its shown 12-bit payload needs deinterleaving, then downstream packing. SPI suffix field order is available.
U14.uncertainty: ADC numeric coding, full SPI packing, stimulation timing and the complete command/USB/frame contract remain open. No firmware implementation is established.

U15.known: The deck associates start-recording with the FPGA clock sent to ASIC.
U15.uncertainty: It does not specify whether stopping that clock is permitted as lossless backpressure or how to resume channel alignment.

U17.known: Chip_Reset and FE_RESET functions are explained; a <1.5 ms reset-time entry is present.
U17.uncertainty: No reset pulse/sequence or compact-board bring-up is defined by the deck.

U18.known: The deck shows earlier ASIC/GUI examples and nominal data/power performance.
U18.uncertainty: This supplies no operating evidence for the compact Artix-7 board, eight-chip capture, XEM8310 link or sustained disk recording.

team_questions.question: Please confirm the current STIM_CLK frequency and edge-time unit: the deck gives 31.25 µs, 32 µs, and 60 kHz. Is 200 Hz permitted, and what STIM_START/CHB timing is required?

Please share the current SPI workbook/generator and corrected full channel map. Slide 26 gives the 12-bit DR suffix and 2124-bit example; we still need the 33-bit stimulus packing, ENABLED treatment, left/right suffix behavior, ADC numeric coding and corrected A49/A57 duplicates.

Please provide a versioned pad/timing table, including AC_IN and IMP_TST, reset polarity/width, input/output limits, clock/data delay and power-on/off states. Can acquisition clocking pause and restart without losing framing?
Please map the actual eight chips and shared clock/SPI/reset groups to the routing-board contacts, and identify who supplies every ASIC analog/digital/stimulation rail and its return.
